text: Synthetic/demo frame feeds MUST be lazy (O(1) memory). The edge 'feed --synthetic N' path originally did render_frames(N * [placement]), which materialises N full board images in a list — at N=100000 that's tens of GB and the container silently hangs/OOMs with no logs (feed only prints on completion). Fix: RepeatSource yields one shared image up to count times lazily (count<=0 / None = forever). Watch for the same trap any time a source pre-builds frames.

Supply-chain 7-day seasoning is enforced via [tool.uv] exclude-newer in the WORKSPACE-ROOT pyproject.toml (resolver setting, applies workspace-wide). Set it to today-minus-7-days; uv then resolves only releases published on/before that date (observed: fastapi 0.137->0.136, pytest 9.1->9.0, starlette 1.3->1.2 rolled back). To take newer deps, bump the date deliberately and re-run 'uv sync' + 'uv run pytest'. The Docker build uses 'uv sync --frozen' so images inherit the same seasoned lock.

The edge/inference layer-separation guard must parse imports with AST, not substring-match the source. A naive 'board_reader_edge not in text' check fails because module DOCSTRINGS legitimately mention the forbidden package ('must never import board_reader_edge'). Use ast.walk over Import/ImportFrom nodes and compare top-level package roots.

opencv-python-headless still needs libglib2.0-0 at runtime on python:3.12-slim-bookworm (otherwise import cv2 fails with libgthread/libglib errors). Install it via apt in the image. The 'headless' variant only drops the GUI/X libs, not glib. Viewer image doesn't use cv2 but installing glib there is harmless with the single parametrised Dockerfile.

Edge rectification round-trip accuracy: auto-detection (find_board_quad: Canny->dilate->largest convex quad) leaves a few-pixel corner error, so the un-warped crop correlates ~0.88 with the original (a thin black border sliver). Manual exact corners clear >0.9. Test thresholds set accordingly: auto round-trip 0.85, manual-corners 0.9. Don't tighten the auto bar without improving detection (e.g. Hough-line clustering / sub-pixel corner refinement, DESIGN A1).

The edge Rectifier suppresses output (RectifyResult.crop=None, status recalibrating/needs_setup) during a bump or when no board is locatable, and FileEdgeAdapter.frames() DROPS suppressed frames rather than forwarding them (DESIGN 4.4.1: a mis-localized crop is confidently-wrong geometry, worse for downstream than an honest gap). The L1->L2 wire Frame has NO status field yet, so edge-originated status is not visible to the inference node — it just sees fewer frames. Plumbing status onto the wire / into status events is deferred to M2/M3.

LiteEmbedder (M1 lightweight square embedder) must NOT be a plain grayscale downsample: the synthetic renderer (sim.render_board) draws white pieces as (245,245,245) on light squares (181,217,240; R=240) -> near-zero grayscale contrast -> white-pieces-on-light-squares classify as 'empty' (self-consistency on the start position drops well below 1.0, only ranks 1-2 wrong). Fix that WORKS (100% per-square through the full rectify+crop+embed+classify pipe on synthetic mid-game boards): per-square subtract the median (background) colour, keep the 3 colour channels of the signed deviation (polarity tells white ink + from black ink -), append a tanh-occupancy bias dim so empty squares stay separable under cosine, then L2-normalize. dim = side*side*3 + 1.

Recognition pipeline wiring: the inference gateway selects its Estimator in server._default_estimator() from the BR_CENTROIDS env var (path to a centroids .npz), resolved at IMPORT time so the uvicorn string-imported 'board_reader_inference.server:app' honours 'serve --centroids' without a code change (the CLI sets os.environ before uvicorn.run). Calibrating from the START position yields all 13/13 class centroids in one frame (it contains every class). The embedding backbone is behind the Embedder protocol (embed.py) per DESIGN 4.6 — LiteEmbedder is the synthetic-only stand-in; DINOv2 (onnxruntime) drops into the same seam for real photos. Calibration takes an ALREADY-RECTIFIED crop (inference must not import edge); rectify first with 'board-reader-edge rectify'.

DINOv2->ONNX export (tools/export_dinov2_onnx.py): use OFFICIAL Meta weights facebook/dinov2-small via transformers AutoModel, wrap to return .pooler_output (the 384-d pooled CLS) so the ONNX has a single 'embedding' output. Gotchas with modern torch (2.x, dynamo exporter): (1) needs 'onnxscript' installed or torch.onnx.export raises ModuleNotFoundError; (2) it prints 'Failed to convert to target version 17 ... No Adapter To Version 17 for Resize' — this is a NON-FATAL opset-downconvert warning; the model is still written at a higher opset and runs fine in onnxruntime 1.26; (3) it spills weights to a sidecar 'model.onnx.data' (model.onnx alone is ~1.5MB!) — consolidate with onnx.load then onnx.save_model(save_as_external_data=False) to get one self-contained ~90MB file. Export tooling (torch/transformers/onnx/onnxscript) lives in an ISOLATED uv project OUTSIDE the workspace (../dinov2-export, CPU torch via pytorch-cpu index) so it never bloats the lean inference runtime; runtime only needs onnxruntime. Input pixel_values[batch,3,224,224] ImageNet-normalised RGB, output embedding[batch,384], dynamic batch.

Real-footage M1 validation (yt streams, operator corner-tap): rectification works on real broadcast frames given 4 corners. Recognition (rectify->crop->embed->centroid) WITHIN-frame self-consistency is strong: video1 start 92% piece/100% occ/98% colour; video2 start 98%/100%/100%. BUT lite and dinov2 embedders TIE on self-consistency because calibrate+classify-the-same-frame is a weak test (each square's centroid includes itself) and is permutation-invariant — it does NOT discriminate backbones. To show DINOv2's value you need a SECOND labeled frame (generalization), i.e. the WP-B4 eval harness. GENERALIZATION (calibrate on start, classify a different mid-game frame) is POOR on these clips: the camera is a very low/side broadcast angle, so tall 3D pieces lean almost horizontally and smear across 1-2 neighbouring squares, breaking the per-square independence the flat-plane homography + centroid assumes. This confirms DESIGN's top risk (per-frame accuracy is the binding constraint) and points to needing a better angle, multi-frame burst voting, or piece-height-aware handling (M2+).
